case_source: (From the judgment and decree dated 13.01.2016 passed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 28 of 2006)
full_judgment:
Zinat Ara J. This Civil Appeal No. 568 of 2016, on leave, has arisen out of judgment and decree dated 13.01.2016 passed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 28 of 2006 making the rule absolute, reversing the judgment and decree dated 14.08.2005 of the 2nd Court of Additional District Judge, Gazipur (briefly, the appellate court) in Title Appeal No. 11 of 2005 allowing the appeal, setting aside the judgment and decree dated 05.01.2005 of the Additional Court No. 1, Senior Assistant Judge, Gazipur (shortly, the trial court) in Title Suit No. 70 of 2002 and dismissing the said suit. The High Court Division by its judgment and decree restored the judgment and decree of the trial court upon setting aside the judgment and decree passed by the appellate court.

<u>Facts of the case</u>

<u>2. Predecessor of respondent Nos.1-23, as plaintiffs, on 06.11.2002 instituted Title Suit No.70 of 2002 before the trial court impleading the appellants as defendants of the said suit. The suit was for declaration that the partition deed No. 5876 dated 07.03.1960 is forged, fraudulent, collusive, illegal, void, without consideration and not acted upon, stating, inter alia, that the land measuring an area of 1.41 acres as described in the schedule to the plaint (hereinafter referred to as the suit property) originally belonged to Gopi Charan Pramanik. Gopi Charan Pramanik sold the suit property to Sheikh Wahed Ali (Wahed Ali), predecessor-in-interest of the plaintiffs, by registered sale deed No. 92 dated 05.01.1924. While Wahed Ali had been in possession of the suit property, he died leaving behind the plaintiffs as his heirs. The plaintiffs were minors at the time of death of Wahed Ali. Therefore, the title documents of the suit property left by Wahed Ali as well as the documents of Moinuddin Munshi, father of Wahed Ali, Chand Ali (Chand Bali) and Amud Ali were in custody of Wahed Ali's step brothers namely, Chand Ali and Amud Ali. They, in collusion with each other, created the impugned deed of partition, wherein the plaintiffs were 1st party and Chand Ali and Amud Ali were 2nd party and 3rd party respectively. Subsequently, Chand Ali and the heirs of Amud Ali filed Title Suit No. 89 of 1989 in the 1st Court of Sub-ordinate Judge, Gazipur for rectification of plot numbers in the deed of partition. Thereafter, the plaintiffs on perusal of the plaint of the said suit came to know about the deed of partition. Then, they obtained a certified copy of the said deed on 29.07.1989 and definitely came to know about the impugned deed of partition. The plaintiffs, as defendants, contested Title Suit No. 89 of 1989 by filing written statement. However, the suit was decreed on contest against the defendant-plaintiffs by judgment and decree dated 08.03.1993. Against the said judgment and decree the plaintiffs of Title Suit NiC). 70 of 2002 i.e. the defendants of Title Suite No. 89 of 1989 preferred First Appeal No. 111 of 1993 before the High Court Division. The High Court Division dismissed the said appeal by judgment and decree dated 10.12.2001 with observations that the plaintiffs ought to have filed a suit for cancellation of the deed of partition. Thereafter, the plaintiffs filed Title Suit No. 70 of 2002 before the trial court.</u>

3. Defendant Nos. 2-11 i.e. the appellants contested the suit stating, inter alia, that Moinuddin, predecessor of the plaintiffs and the defendants, died leaving three sons, Wahed Ali, Chand Ali (Chand Bali) and Amud Ali. Wahed Ali was the eldest son and so, he used to supervise the joint family affairs. He purchased the suit property by joint earning of all the brother; but the kabala was registered in his name alone. Wahed Ali as elder brother partitioned the suit property in three parts and delivered possession to his two brothers when they started living separately. Therefore, all the brothers had/have been possessing the suit property dividing the same equally in three parts and erecting separate houses in their respective shares on Plot No. 1008 and they have also been living therein since the lifetime of Wahed Ali. Subsequently, after the death of Wahed Ali dispute started between the heirs of Wahed Ali, Chand Ali and Amud Ali. Whereupon, the relatives and local elites settled the matter amicably.

Thereupon, the impugned deed of parti-tion was executed by heirs of Wahed Ali and. Wahed Ali's two brothers Chand Ali and Amud Ali. Hamida Banu and Chandra Banu, two daughters of Wahed Ali sold their shares to Nurul Islam. Rahimon Nessa sold her share to her two brothers, Abbas Ali and Rahmat Ali. Abbas Ali transferred his 29/41 decimals land to Nurul Islam. Omar Ali, 4 Plaintiff No. 4, transferred 17/40 decimals land to Rafiqul admitting the disputed deed of partition. The defendants have been possessing and living in their part of suit property for more than 43/44 years. The suit is not maintainable and hopelessly barred by limitation. The defendants prayed for dismissal of the suit.

4. The following Issues The following issues were framed by the trial Court for deciding the suit:

বিচার্য বিষয় সমূহ

১। বর্তমান আকারে মামলাটি আইনত চলে কি?

২। মামলাটি তামাদি দোষে বারিত কি?

৩। নালিশী বন্টন নামা দলিল তঞ্চকী, যোগ সাজসী, বে-আইনী এবং বাতিল যোগ্য কি?

৪। প্রার্থীত মতে বাদী পক্ষ ডিক্রী পাইতে হকদার কি?

Trial and Decision of Trial Court

5. The plaintiffs examined three witnesses in support of their case and the defendants examined one witness in support of their case. Both the parties produced some documents in support of their respective cases and those were marked as exhibits. The trial court on consideration of the evidence on record decreed Title Suit No. 70 of 2002 in favour of the plaintiffs by judgment and decree dated 05.01.2005 and declared the deed of partition as fraudulent and illegal. The trial court also directed the concerned Sub-registrar to note about cancellation of the deed of partition in relevant column of the register.

Appeal and decision of the appellate court

6. Feeling aggrieved, the defendant-appellants filed an appeal in the Court of District Judge. The said appeal being Title Appeal No. 11 of 2005 was heard by the 2nd Court of Additional District Judge, Gazipur. The appellate court by judgment and decree dated 14.08.2005 allowed the appeal on contest against plaintiff-respondent Nos. 1-16 and ex-parte against the rest. It set aside the judgment and decree passed by the trial court and dismissed Title Suit No. 70 of 2002.

Revision before the High Court Division and result

7. Feeling aggrieved, the plaintiffs of Title Suit No. 70 of 2002 preferred Civil Revision No. 28 of 2006 before the High Court Division. The High Court Division, upon hearing, by judgment and decree dated 13.01.2016 made the rule absolute and set aside the judgment and decree of the appellate court and restored the judgment and decree passed by the trial court in Title Suit No. 70 of 2002.

Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal and the appeal

8. Being aggrieved, the leave petitioners, appellants herein, preferred Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 2214 of 2016 and leave was granted to consider the following ground:

"Because the High Court Division has not reversed any material findings of the judgment and decree of the Court of appeal and the without applying the judgment and decree of the appellate Court thereby committed an error of law causing gross miscarriage of justice."

9. This appeal is the result of the aforesaid civil petition.

Arguments of the appellants side

10. Mr. Serajur Rahman, the learned Advocate-on-Record appearing for the appellants, has taken us through the judgment and decree passed by the trial court, the appellate court, the High Court Division, the connected materials on record and has put forward the following arguments before us:

I. Admittedly, the appellants and their predecessors i.e. the defendants of Title Suit No. 70 of 2002 previously filed Title Suit No, 89 of 1989 for rectification of plot numbers the impugned deed of partition being No.5876 dated 07.03,1960. The present respondent-plaintiffs as defendants of the said suit in their written statement clearly stated that they came to know about the impugned partition deed definitely upon obtaining certified copy of the said deed on 29.07.1989. Thus, the defendants of the said suit and plaintiffs of Title Suit No. 70 of 2002 had definite knowledge about the impugned deed of partition as per their own admission since 29.07.1989.

II. But they did not file any suit challenging the said deed of partition within a long period of more than 12 years. Rather, after the suit was decreed on contest against the defendants of Title Suit No. 89 of 1989 they firstly filed First Appeal No. 111 of 1993 in the High Court Division, which was dismissed and then they filed the instant suit in the year 2002. Therefore, the suit was/is hopelessly barred by limitation, in view of the provision of Article 91 of the Limitation Act, 1908. The appellate court legally decided the issue of limitation against the plaintiffs of Title Suit No. 70 of 2002. But the High Court Division without considering the facts and circumstances of the case erroneously decided that the suit was not barred by limitation.

III. Admittedly, the plaintiffs are not in possession of the major area of the suit property. Rather, Chand Ali and the heirs of Amud Ali i.e. the defendant-appellants are in possession of major area of the suit property since the lifetime of Wahed Ali by virtue of amicable partition and then by virtue of the impugned deed of partition by erecting their homestead thereon at least for the last 40-44 years.

IV. In the previous suit filed by the appellants, the High Court Division clearly observed that the appellants have been in possession of the suit property since the lifetime of Sheikh Wahed Ali. The defendants failed to succeed up to High Court Division with their written statement case, which is similar to the plaint of Title Suit No. 70 of 2002. As Chand Ali and the heirs of Amud Ali i.e. the defendants of the suit have been admittedly in possession of major part of the suit property for a long period of at least 43-44 years, a simple suit for declaration that the impugned deed of partition is fraudulent and illegal without praying for declaration of title of the plaintiffs to the suit property and for recovery of khas possession thereof is not maintainable. The appellate court legally decided the said issue but the High Court Division without considering the aforesaid admitted facts and circumstances of the case erroneously allowed the revision and restored the unlawful judgment and decree passed by the trial court.

V. The High Court Division did not reverse the material findings of the judgment and decree of the appellate court, the court for final determination on facts. The High Court Division has not also observed that there has been any misreading or non-consideration of the evidence on record, resulting in an error of law and High Court Division without considering" the said matters erroneously allowed the revision and set aside the legal judgment and decree of the appellate court and restored the unlawful judgment and decree of the trial court. Therefore, the judgment and decree of the High Court Division is erroneous and liable to be set aside. Arguments of the respondents side In reply, Mr. Abdur Rahman, the learned Advocate for the plaintiff-respondents contends as under:

a) Before rectification of the deed of partition and correction of C.S. Plot Nos. 103 and 108 to C.S. Plot Nos. 1003 and 1008, the plaintiffs had no cause of action for the suit inasmuch as, they had no apprehension of being aggrieved so as to file a suit. b) The judgment in First Appeal No. 111 of 1993 was pronounced on 10.12.2001 affirming rectification of C.S. Plot Nos. 1003 and 1008 in place of 103 and 108 in the impugned deed of partition and so, the cause of action of plaintiffs to file a suit arose firstly on that date and not prior to it. Therefore, the plaintiffs having filed the suit within three years from the date of cause of action, the suit was/is not barred by limitation under Article 91 of the Limitation Act, 1908. So, the trial court as well as the High Court Division lawfully decided that the suit is not barred by limitation. c) Although, the defendant-appellants may be in possession of part of the suit property but the same starts from the lifetime of Wahed Ali and so, the defendants failed to prove that the impugned deed of partition was acted upon. d) The defendants also failed to prove that the suit property was purchased in the name of Wahed Ali with the joint income of three brothers. Thus, the suit for simple declaration that the impugned deed of partition is forged, fraudulent, unlawful, not acted upon, etc. is the proper relief for the plaintiffs and further declaration of their title to the suit property as well as recovery of khas possession is not necessary. e) The plaintiffs' predecessor in interest Wahed Ali had purchased the suit property in the year 1924 and he was the sole owner of the same. The heirs of Wahed Ali were minors at the time of death of Wahid Ali and so Wahed Ali's step brothers had been in possession of the relevant documents of Wahed Ali. f) At the time of execution of the deed of partition, the plaintiffs were minors. The said facts are also proved by some of the witnesses. Thus, the deed of partition is apparently fraudulent and illegal.

g) On consideration of evidence on record, the suit was lawfully decreed by the trial Court and affirmed by the High Court Division in favour of the plaintiffs. The appellate court unlawfully decided the issues in favour of the defendants and against the plaintiffs. The appeal is thus, liable to be dismissed.

11. However, Mr. Abdur Rahman finds it difficult to satisfy as to how the suit could be treated as maintainable without any consequential prayer for recovery of khas possession although the other side had/have been admittedly in possession of the major part in the suit property.

Examination of Records

12. We have examined the judgment and decree of various courts relating to the suit property and the evidence on record.

Deliberation of the Court

13. Admittedly, the appellants had previously filed Title Suit No. 89 of 1989 for rectification of the impugned deed of partition so far as it relates to C.S. Plot Nos. 1003 and 1008 and it was decreed in their favour. The defendants of that suit then preferred First Appeal No. 111 of 1993 before the High Court Division and it was dismissed by the High Court Division. From the judgment of the High Court Division it appears that it has been clearly observed therein by the said Division as under:

We have heard both the sides and examined documents and evidence adduce by the parties. Admittedly, the partition deed in question was executed by the defendants by going to the Sub-Registry Office, Gazipur, obviously with full knowledge that a deed was executed and registered on 7.3.1960 (Exhibit-1). The said deed has never been challenged by the defendants in any suit seeking cancellation of the deed with the allegation of fraud, undue influence, etc. under section 39 of the Specific Relief Act. Where a written instrument is void ab anitio/ab initio, the transaction is nullity, the document does not require to be cancelled and the party can avoid it even as defendants in suit of the present nature brought by others. But in the present case, the defendants being admitted executants of the deed, the same is only avoidable at the option of executing parties. As such it is incumbent upon the defendants to have it cancelled or set aside by filing a suit under section 39 of the Specific Relief Act, 1877. It is an absurd proposition of the learned Advocate for the appellant to bring amendment in the written statement seeking such cancellation as defendants in this suit. The defendant cannot get decree for such relief in the instituted by their adversaries. Therefore, the submission of the learned Advocate for the Appellants is totally without sub-stance. It is also an admitted fact that the insertion of the plot Nos. 103 and 108 in the disputed partition deed was an advertent mistake. None of the parties or their predecessors had or have any interest in respect of lands involved in those two plots. At the time of hearing before us, the learned Advocate for the appellant side conceded that insertion of those two plots in the deed was a mistake occurred inadvertently. But the defendants want to resist correction of the deed to remove admitted error challenging the validity of the partition deed itself. But in a suit of the present nature, the defendants cannot get any relief by way of the cancellation of the partition deed in question as we have stated above. The plaintiffs, in fact, filed the suit in a declaratory form seeking simple declaration that the two plot numbers in the partition deed were wrongly inserted. Since the suit was for declaration under section 42 of the Specific Relief Act such a simple declaration about the incorrectness of the plot numbers in the deed was not adequate to get proper relief in the matter. Because the deed in question would remain incorrect as before in spite of such declaration. So, correction of the deed in question is the proper relief which ought to have been asked for by the plaintiffs as a consequential relief. However, the plaintiff-respondents got their plaint amended before the appellate court on 04.12.2001 seeking such consequential relief in the form of making correction of the document by the concerned Sub-register. Requisite Court fees have also been paid. In view of such amendment, the defect has already been cured and there is no bar to maintain the suit for simple correction of the document.   In consequence of mistake in writing plot numbers, shares of the partition shown the R.S. Khatian are wrong. So, we do not find any legality in the second declaration allowed by the Court below. It may be mentioned that witnesses of both sides admitted possession of the plaintiffs and defendants in the suit land. Having due regard to the aforesaid facts, circumstances and evidences on record, we find that the plaintiffs are entitled to get the impugned partition deed corrected and also get declaration as given by the court below. There is no ground to disagree with the learned trial court in this respect. However, in view of subsequent amendment in the plaint on 04.12.2001, we are inclined to modify the ordering portion of the judgment in an appropriate manner."

14. From the above observation and decision of the High Court Division in the previous appeal being No. 111 of 1993, it is clear that the High Court Division on consideration of the evidence on record found that the present appellants and respondents i.e. both parties, have been in possession of the suit property since Wahed Ali's lifetime and that none of the parties or their predecessors had or has any interest in respect of lands involved in those two plots and that the mistake was also admitted by both parties, while allowing rectification of the disputed partition deed.

15. Admittedly, the defendants i.e. the plaintiffs of Title Suit No. 70 of 2002 contested the said suit. Therefore, they had full knowledge about the suit property as the boundary of the suit property was mentioned clearly in the said deed with khatian numbers, etc. Only there was some inadvertent mistake in writing down the plot numbers i.e. C.S. Plot Nos. 103 and 108 were written in place of C.S. Plot Nos. 1003 and 1008. Therefore, when the plaintiffs allegedly came to know about the deed of partition in the said suit i.e. in the year 1989, they had definite knowledge about the deed of partition but they have not filed the suit for cancellation of the said deed or any declaration that the impugned deed of partition is fraudulent, illegal, etc. Rather, they had prayed for cancellation of said deed as defendants by way of amendment of the written statement. Therefore, it is evident that the cause of action for the suit arose in the year 1989 but the plaintiffs have filed Title Suit No. 70 of 2002 for declaration that the deed of partition is forged, fraudulent collusive, not acted upon, etc. in the year 2002 i.e. more than 12 years after. Thus, in view of the provision of Article 91 of the Limitation Act, 1908 the suit having not filed within a period of three years from the date of knowledge is hopelessly barred by limitation.

<u>16. It be mentioned that the High Court Division in First Appeal No. 111 of 1993 has not directed the plaintiffs to file any suit for cancellation of the deed of partition. But just an observation was given that, "As such it is incumbent upon the defendants to have it cancelled or set aside by filing a suit under the Specific Relief Act." In the said appeal it was not also considered as to whether the suit seeking cancellation of the deed of partition or declaration that the deed of partition is forged, etc. would be barred by limitation although the defendant-plaintiffs had definite knowledge about the deed of partition in the year 1989.</u>

17. In view of the discussion made hereinbefore, it is evident that the suit was/is hopelessly barred by limitation. The appellate court correctly decided this issue. But the trial court as well as the High Court Division, without considering the actual date of definite knowledge of the plaintiffs in the year 1989 and the provision of Article 91 of the Limitation Act, 1908 erroneously decided that the suit is not barred by limitation.

18. The other questions raised by the appellants side is about the maintainability of the suit itself as well as other issues involved in the suit.

19. In Title Suit No. 70 of 2002 the plaintiffs only sought for declaration that the impugned deed of partition is forged, fraudulent, collusive, illegal, void and not acted upon.

20. From the judgment of the High Court Division in First Appeal No.111 of 1993 it is evident that admittedly three brothers Wahed Ali, Chand All and Amud Ali had been living in the suit property by erecting three separate houses since the lifetime of Wahed Ali. Therefore, the trial court as well as the High Court Division failed to consider that three separate houses of Wahed Ali, Chand Ali (Chand Bali) and Amud Ali were erected when the Wahed Ali was alive. It clearly shows that the owners of the suit property were three brothers for which three brothers/ their heirs had/have been living there by erecting three separate houses. Unless the suit property was owned by three brothers, there was no earthly reason for the other two brothers of Wahed Ali to construct/erect separate houses on it. The deed of partition was just a recognition the same. Further, admittedly the deed of partition was also executed by the mother of the plaintiffs. She, being mother of several children, was no doubt a major. This fact is admitted by the learned advocate for the respondents. This shows that the claim that all the executants of the impugned partition deed were minors is not true. Moreover, the suit was not also filed by the alleged minor- plaintiffs after their attaining majority, although they had executed the deed of partition in the year 1960, as it appears from the judgment of the High Court Division in First Appeal No. 111 of 1993. It appears that the appellate court in consideration of the statement of witnesses, written statement filed by the defendant-appellants decided as under:

From the evidence given by the P.W.s it appears that they wanted to prove that the plaintiffs were minors at the time of execution of the disputed partition deed but it does not appear to me that the plaintiffs have come out successful in proving the said story. It is admitted by the P.W. 1 that defendant Nos. 13-15 are living at Village Dhirashram whose husbands name was not mentioned in the pliant but their husbands name is found to be mentioned in the partition deed in question. The female members of our society normally get acquaintance of their own by the name of their husband. The plaintiff Nos. 13-15 are no doubt married but it is not intelligible to me why their husbands name was not mentioned in the plaint. In the facts and circumstances it appears to me that the device has been adopted by the plaintiffs to strengthen their plea of their minority which do not got support from the evidence on record. At the time of appeal hearing learned Advocate for the plaintiff-Respondents drew my attention to the statement made in para 'Uma' of the W/S and submitted that the question of minority of the heirs of Wahed Ali is found to be admitted. For better understanding I want to reproduce the relevant potion of the W/S which runs as “বন্টননামা দলিল হওয়ার সময় ওহেদ আলীর ওয়ারিশগন নাবালক ছিল। উহা সঠিক নয় ওহেদ আলীর ওয়ারিশগন নাবালক ছিল যাহা উক্ত বন্টননামায় উহার স্বত্ব প্রমান করিবে। ওহেদ আলীর মেয়ে হামিদা ভানু ও চন্দু ভানু এবং রহমত আলীর মেয়েরা বিবাহিত থাকা সত্ত্বেও চালাকি করিয়া আরজিতে তাহাদের স্বামীর নাম উল্লেখ না করিয়া বরং পিতার নাম উল্লেখ করিয়াছে।”

On careful perusal of the statement it does not appear to me that the question of minority of the heirs of Wahed Ali has been admitted. This complicity appears to have cropped up on account of not putting punctuation mark in right place. However the question of minority of the 1st party to the disputed deed does not appear to be admitted by the defendants. Therefore, the decision recorded by the learned trial Judge as to the minority of the 1st party to the deed cannot be accepted….”

21. On the other hand, while deciding Civil Revision No. 28 of 2006 the High Court Division decided as follows:

"On the question of minority of the heirs of Wahed Ali nothing has been said excepting the daughters of Wahed Ali at that time were not minors, as they were married. It appears that the fact of this case, let me took to the fact in earlier century, at the time, minors were given marriage. But nothing has been said about minority of the heirs of Wahed Ali. Under section 101 of the Evidence Act to prove the fact i.e. at that time daughters of Wahed Ali were minors onus is upon defendant but defendant save and except the fact that daughters were married, no other evidences were brought to the Court. This finding of trial court has been reversed by the court of appeal below simply by stroke of pen on taking into consideration that defendant did not admit the daughters of Wahed Ali were minor at the time entering into contract. I find that excepting statement made in the written statement defendant did not brought on record any evidence to prove that the daughters of Wahed Ali were major. Law says that contract by minor is not legal. I find substance in the rule."

22. We failed to understand what the High Court Division meant by the aforesaid observations and decision.

23. The provision of Article 101 of the Evidence Act, 1872 reads as under:

"101. Burden of proof -Whoever desires any Court to give judgment as to any legal right or liability dependent on the existence of facts which he asserts, must prove that those facts exist. When a person is bound to prove the existence of any fact, it is said that the burden of proof lies on that person."

24. It be mentioned that the plaintiffs claim that they were minors at the time of execution of the impugned deed of partition. Therefore, the burden of proof was upon the plaintiffs to prove that they were minors at the time of execution of the impugned deed of partition.

25. The plaintiffs have not stated their dates of birth in the plaint. The evidence shows that the plaintiffs have not filed any documentary evidence to prove their date of birth, so as to ascertain their actual date of birth.

<u>26. The general principle of law is that the plaintiff must prove its suit otherwise the suit would fail.</u>

27. The appellate court, i.e. the final fact finding court, in consideration of the evidence on record with reasons decided that the plaintiffs failed to prove that they were minors at the time of execution of the impugned deed of partition.

28. The High Court Division while deciding civil revision did not point out any misreading on non-consideration of the evidence on record by the appellate court. Therefore, the High Court Division without reversing the material findings of the appellate court reversed the judgment and decree of dismissal of the suit by the appellate court, which is not proper.

29. Now let us turn our eye on maintainability of the suit.

30. At the outset, it be mentioned that in the judgment of First Appeal No.111 of 1993 the High Court Division has not considered the issue if a simple suit for declaration, that the impugned partition deed is fraudulent, illegal etc., without any consequential relief would be maintainable.

<u>31. Be that as it may, on perusal of the judgment of the appellate court in Title Appeal No.11 of 2005 it appears that the appellate court considering the evidence on record correctly decided that the defendants have been in possession in the suit property since the lifetime of Wahed Ali. Therefore, the present suit for declaration that deed of partition is fraudulent, collusive etc. without any prayer for a decree for recovery of khas possession is not maintainable. Because, even if the document is declared fraudulent and illegal and the document is also cancelled, as has been done by the trial court and the High Court Division, the plaintiffs would not be entitled to get recovery of khas possession of the part of the suit property which had/have been admittedly in possession of the defendant-appellants. Therefore, the suit for declaration that the impugned partition deed is fraudulent and illegal and cancellation of the deed without any prayer for consequential relief i.e. declaration of title to the suit property and recovery of khas possession of the part of the suit property in which the plaintiffs are not in possession, is not also maintainable. But the trial court has not considered this legal issue correctly and the trial court erroneously decreed the suit. The High Court Division without reversing any material findings of the appellate court made the rule absolute, set aside the judgment and decree of dismissal of the (CIF Rtsuit g-y the appellate court and restored the erroneous judgment and decree of the trial court.</u>

32. Therefore, the High Court Division committed an error of law occasioning failure of justice and, as such, the judgment and decree passed by the High Court Division is liable to be interfered with.

33. In view of the above, we find merit in the appeal.

34. Accordingly, the appeal is allowed without any order as to costs.

35. The judgment and decree of the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 28 of 2006 is hereby set aside and the judgment and decree dated 14.08.2005 passed by the 2nd Court of Additional District Judge, Gazipur in Title Appeal No. 11 of 2005 is hereby restored and Title Suit No. 70 of 2002 of the Additional Court No. 1, Senior Assistant Judge, Gazipur is dismissed.

End.
